From: Luca Bianchi <luca.bianchi@europabank.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: security@europabank.com; auditor@grantthornton.com
Date: Fri, 14 Jun 2028 09:12:00 +0200
Subject: CAIQ evidence intake & control justification — Europa Bank audit

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for taking this on. As part of our upcoming due diligence (live audit window: 2028-06-25 to 2028-06-27) the audit team has asked for a CAIQ response package and sampled artifacts that map to high-priority controls across the Cloud Controls Matrix (we highlighted 12 controls; primary asks below). We need: a short justification for any non-standard control responses, 1–2 representative artifacts per control (logs, configs, policy excerpts), and guidance on any items that require secure transfer.

Priority controls (examples):
- CCM-ENCR-01: key management and rotation evidence
- CCM-LOG-04: runtime access logs for inference endpoints (30-day window)
- CCM-ACCESS-07: privileged access attestations and least-privilege rationale

Can you confirm the owner for each control, the planned artifact for sampling, and whether anything is restricted (PII/keys) so we can schedule the secure handoff? Attaching our intake spreadsheet with the auditor's fields: CAIQ_answers_v1.xlsx (stub).

Appreciate a two-business-day turnaround if possible.

Best,
Luca
Head of Technology Risk — Europa Bank

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Luca Bianchi <luca.bianchi@europabank.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 14 Jun 2028 10:03:00 +0200
Subject: Re: CAIQ evidence intake & control justification — Europa Bank audit

Luca —

Thanks for the clear asks and timeline. We can support the 25–27 June window. High-level plan below and an initial artifact index attached (CAIQ-evidence-index-20280614.csv).

Plan (high level):
1) Control owners confirmed and artifacts inventoried (today — internal owners listed below).
2) Sensitive artifacts (keys, HSM exports) will be staged via a secure share and only accessible to the auditor's approved accounts.
3) Log extraction run and sampling window: Jonas will run a 30-day extraction for inference/runtime logs and provide a redact-and-sample package.
4) Delivery: Audit handoff on 2028-06-21 (technical runbook walk-through), formal artifact push 2028-06-24 via SFTP/secure drive.

Initial control owner roster (samples):
- CCM-ENCR-01 (key rotation): kimberly_park (owner) — artifact: rotation policy + rotation audit records
- CCM-LOG-04 (runtime logs): jonas_weber (owner) — artifact: redacted logs, extraction notes
- CCM-ACCESS-07 (privileged access): grace_oconnor (owner) — artifact: privileged access list + attestation emails

Open question for the auditors: do they require raw HSM key material? Our standard approach is to provide KMS/HSM rotation logs, key identifiers, and attestation statements — not key material. If they insist, we need a formal exception and a legal/Compliance sign-off.

I attached the CSV index for the controls we're starting with. Kimberly, Grace, Jonas — can you confirm the artifact files you intend to hand off and whether any need a redaction step? We plan the technical handoff call on 2028-06-21 at 09:00 CET.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Security Program Manager — Redwood Inference

Attachments: CAIQ-evidence-index-20280614.csv (stub)

Marissa / Luca —

Confirming ownership for CCM-ENCR-01. Planned artifacts:
- encryption_key_rotation_policy.pdf (policy excerpt; will redact internal contact details)
- kms_rotation_audit_2028Q2.csv (rotation events; will redact ARN fragments where necessary)

Note on sensitive items: Key material will not be provided. We can provide KMS/HSM attestations, rotation timestamps, and HSM export logs that indicate operation IDs. If GT requires additional proof, we'll need a signed request and engagement with our Legal team.

Also: there are several SOC 2 artifacts that overlap. To avoid redundant pulls, I propose we mark overlap controls in the CSV (column: "overlap_source": SOC2). This will save us time during the sprint.

Question for auditors (cc Luca): for the runtime sampling window, do you need full HTTP headers or is endpoint-level metadata sufficient? Endpoint headers contain internal customer identifiers that we'd prefer to redact.

Kimberly Park
Security Engineering Lead — Redwood Inference
